questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes data mining from a standard database query?
options: Data mining requires SQL; queries use Python
A query retrieves known facts; data mining discovers unknown patterns
Data mining only works on structured data; queries work on all data
Queries are faster; data mining is slower
questions.explanation: A SQL query retrieves facts you already knew to ask for. Data mining discovers structure you did not know was there — patterns, clusters, rules, anomalies.

questions.text: In the KDD process, which step consumes roughly 80% of project time?
questions.explanation: Steps 1–3 of KDD (Selection, Preprocessing, Transformation) — collectively called data preparation — consume roughly 80% of project time. The actual algorithm application is a relatively small fraction of the effort.

questions.text: Which of the 4 Vs of Big Data refers to the trustworthiness and quality of data?
questions.explanation: Veracity refers to the trustworthiness and quality of data — including noise, missing values, outliers, and entry errors. The course dataset intentionally introduces Veracity challenges.

questions.text: The fraud_flag target has ~3% positive cases. A classifier that always predicts 'no fraud' achieves:
questions.explanation: The naïve classifier correctly labels all 97% non-fraud records — achieving 97% accuracy — but it misses every actual fraud (0% recall). This is why accuracy alone is misleading for rare-event classification.

questions.text: Clustering is a supervised learning task because it assigns observations to groups.
questions.explanation: Clustering is unsupervised — there are no predefined class labels. The algorithm discovers natural groupings in the data without any labelled training examples.
